claims.claim: Samsung proposes transmitter error vector magnitude (EVM) limits of 2.5% at 4 GHz and 2.8% at 7 GHz for fixed wireless access (FWA) uplink 1024-point quadrature amplitude modulation (1024-QAM).
claims.passage:
Based on the above, 2.5% for 4GHz and 2.8% for 7GHz should be agreed as the Tx EVM for FWA UL 1024QAM, including LO phase noise, IQ imbalance and carrier leakage. Both values are proven in the RAN4 LLS, can be supported with a practical back-off, and are aligned with the BS Tx EVM for DL 1024QAM.
Proposal 1: The Tx EVM for FWA 4GHz UL 1024QAM is 2.5%, including LO phase noise, IQ imbalance and carrier leakage.
Proposal 2: The Tx EVM for FWA 7GHz UL 1024QAM is 2.8%, including LO phase noise, IQ imbalance and carrier leakage.

claims.claim: Ericsson instead proposes 2.5% at both frequencies. Its submission puts a competing option before Radio Access Network Working Group 4 (RAN4): one transmitter-error limit across both frequencies.
claims.passage:
Based on the discussion in the previous sections we propose the following:
Proposal 1	Adopt a UE Tx EVM of 2.5% for UL 1024QAM for FWA for both 4 GHz and 7 GHz.
Proposal 2	UL 1024QAM for FWA is supported without a restriction on the number of MIMO layers.

claims.claim: Samsung compares the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at which 1024-QAM begins to outperform 256-QAM with the output power recovered by relaxing transmitter EVM. It argues that each candidate limit should be judged by comparing the change in crossover SNR with the change in power back-off.
claims.passage: For the down-selection, two aspects need to be considered together. The first is the gain of UL 1024QAM shown in the RAN4 LLS, i.e., the SNR (or SINR) at which UL 1024QAM starts to outperform UL 256QAM (crossover SNR). The second is the output power cost of the Tx EVM. Although the MPR is postponed to the WI phase, the Tx EVM agreed in the SI sets the PA linearity needed and hence the MPR to be specified later. As shown in [5], only the PA part of the Tx EVM changes with output power, by about 2dB for each 1dB of back-off, while the other parts, e.g., LO phase noise, do not. In other words, a tighter PA contribution costs about 1dB of back-off per 2dB of EVM, and a relaxed PA contribution saves back-off at the same rate. Therefore, each Tx EVM candidate should be judged by comparing the change in the crossover SNR with the change in back-off.

claims.claim: For 4 GHz, Samsung reports that relaxing transmitter EVM from 2.5% to 2.8% raises the crossover SNR by about 3 decibels in the single-layer cases it discusses. Under its assumed distortion budget, it estimates only about 0.9 decibels of recovered output power, and argues that the relaxation reduces the net gain.
claims.passage:
For 4GHz, the averaged LLS results from companies in RAN4#119 are shown in Figure 1 [3]. Between 2.5%+2.5% and 2.8%+2.5% (Tx EVM + Rx EVM), only the Tx EVM is changed, so this pair directly shows the impact of the Tx EVM. For all Rank 1 cases, the crossover SNR increases by about 3dB (2.7dB to 3.7dB) when the Tx EVM is relaxed from 2.5% to 2.8%, e.g., from 23.7dB to 26.7dB for MCS23 in TDL-D. For Rank 2 in TDL-A, the crossover SNR increases from about 31dB to about 46dB, which is beyond the practical SNR range of FWA. A similar trend is shown in [4], where the crossover SNR for MCS24 increases by 1.5dB to 2.8dB from 2.5%+2.5% to 3%+2.3%. In other words, at 4GHz the crossover SNR is very sensitive to the Tx EVM, and the gain of UL 1024QAM is clearly achieved within a practical SNR range with 2.5% Tx EVM.
Figure 1: Averaged crossover SINR of UL 1024QAM over UL 256QAM (MCS22), 4GHz, 1T4R [3]
On the other hand, the back-off saved by relaxing the 4GHz Tx EVM from 2.5% to 2.8% is small. Assuming about 1% each for the transceiver non-linearity, LO phase noise and IQ imbalance at 4GHz, the PA contribution is about 1.8% for 2.5% Tx EVM and grows only to about 2.2% for 2.8% Tx EVM, i.e., by about 1.7dB. At the rate of about 1dB of back-off per 2dB of EVM, this saves only about 0.9dB of back-off. A 0.9dB higher output power can give at most a 0.9dB higher SNR at the BS, which is much smaller than the about 3dB increase of the crossover SNR. Therefore, relaxing the 4GHz Tx EVM from 2.5% to 2.8% reduces the net gain of UL 1024QAM rather than making UL 1024QAM easier to use.

claims.claim: At 7 GHz, Samsung argues for 2.8% to accommodate larger power-amplifier and local-oscillator contributions while preserving more modulation gain than 3%. Its calculation assumes about 1.2% local-oscillator phase noise.
claims.passage: At 7GHz, both the PA and LO contributions are larger than at 4GHz. PA gain and linearity generally degrade at higher frequency, so more PA distortion is expected at the same output power, and LO phase noise also increases with the carrier frequency. Assuming about 1.2% LO phase noise at 7GHz, compared with about 1% at 4GHz, and the same transceiver non-linearity and IQ imbalance as at 4GHz, a 2.5% Tx EVM at 7GHz would require the PA contribution to be reduced to about 1.7%. This is even tighter than about 1.8% at 4GHz despite the worse PA linearity, and costs about 1dB more back-off than 2.8% Tx EVM. With 2.8% Tx EVM, the PA contribution is about 2.1%, so the higher LO contribution is covered and some margin is also given to the PA. In other words, 2.8% for 7GHz covers the higher PA and LO contributions, while it keeps the MPR at about the same level as at 4GHz. A further relaxation to 3% saves only about 0.5dB of back-off, since the PA contribution grows only to about 2.36%, i.e., by about 1dB. Even if a larger LO contribution of about 1.5% is assumed at 7GHz, the back-off saved by the relaxation to 3% is only about 0.6dB. This is smaller than the about 1dB or more increase of the crossover SNR. Therefore, 2.8% is a reasonable Tx EVM for 7GHz.

claims.claim: Ericsson argues that one EVM limit avoids separate maximum power reduction (MPR) sets and a frequency boundary. It says a frequency-dependent limit would require two MPR sets and corresponding conformance tests, whereas one limit would allow a single set per device power class and waveform.
claims.passage:
In NR, the UE MPR is specified per power class and waveform and does not depend on the operating band. For higher-order modulation, the MPR is driven by the Tx EVM requirement. A frequency-dependent UE Tx EVM, e.g. following the BS DL 1024QAM split at 4.2 GHz in TS 38.104 [8], would require two sets of MPR for UL 1024QAM and the corresponding conformance tests. It would also require a frequency boundary: with 4.2 GHz, the 4400-4800 MHz range studied in TR 38.922 would fall in a different category than the 4 GHz evaluations. A single value avoids these issues and results in one MPR set per power class and waveform for all bands. Furthermore, four sources show that the MPR increase for 2.5% Tx EVM is limited to 0.5-1.5 dB, whether compared with the existing NR 256QAM MPR or with a more relaxed 1024QAM Tx EVM [3]-[6].
NR UE MPR is specified per power class and waveform, independent of the operating band. A single UL 1024QAM Tx EVM for 4 GHz and 7 GHz results in a single MPR set per power class and waveform, whereas a frequency-dependent Tx EVM requires two MPR sets and a frequency boundary.

claims.claim: Ericsson also proposes leaving the number of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) layers unrestricted. It argues that link adaptation selects transmission rank and modulation together, so multilayer transmission need not be scheduled when the channel or base-station configuration cannot support it.
claims.passage:
Furthermore, the aNB selects UL rank and MCS together through link adaptation, therefore multi-layer is simply not scheduled when channel condition or the BS configuration do not support it. Therefore, it is proposed not to restrict MIMO layers to UL 1024QAM.
UL 1024QAM for FWA is supported without a restriction on the number of MIMO layers.

claims.claim: Samsung says that choosing transmitter EVM during the study sets the power-amplifier linearity needed and hence constrains the power reduction to be specified later.
claims.passage: Although the MPR is postponed to the WI phase, the Tx EVM agreed in the SI sets the PA linearity needed and hence the MPR to be specified later.

claims.claim: The exact MPR, Samsung says, will be decided in the work-item phase.
claims.passage: The exact MPR will be decided in the WI phase.
